# Revised Super User architecture — document-only review package

2026-10-08, Asia/Singapore. **Revised design, not implemented controls or an accepted harness stage.**

The human accepted META-01 and directed elimination of pathname-marker authorization, exact transactional access auditing, exact basic account support, preserved U-01 public behavior, and operation-level relationship authorization. Those directions are incorporated below. No Super User feature source, supplementary product tests, schema, database, harness gate or frozen fixture is changed.

Target **T/**: `C:/Users/kirby/Desktop/lms-monorepo-skeleton/.orchestra/runs/controlled-superuser-20261004/task`. Source digest remains `9c4cc7834a8615bfad1b11fe243287a49af292a866103dfe7e0de50b3922a1af`; current run `run_superuser_20261004` remains DRAFT/HIGH, next requirements, no lease or implementation approval. Docker/Sandbox repair stays closed; Calendar and deployment work are excluded.

The seven original frozen fixture hashes, original 28 reviewer findings and their genuine receipts remain unchanged. This package supersedes design choices in 002/007, not the historical contents of their hash-bound review packets. Fresh reviewers must use this revision, not silently reuse old-session conclusions.

## Package and evidence

- [Complete intended boundary matrix](008-revised-boundary-matrix.json): all 120 route files, 171 declared/aliased HTTP operations, 59 exported/inline/service operations and 78 dashboard page/layout files. Each operation has entry point, actual actor, role set, institute, persisted relationship, denial/effect ordering, source hash and unique future case ID. This is design completeness, not independent review coverage or product execution.
- [Exact revised source/file allowlist](008-revised-file-allowlist.json): 220 existing modification-eligible files and 13 explicit future product files; no new source is written. Public leaderboard and middleware are review-only, unchanged. One client page has an explicit future extraction/server-wrapper pair. No unlisted path may change without revised adjudication/plan review.
- [Every original finding's revision disposition](008-finding-by-finding-adjudication.json): preserves each independent finding ID/severity/evidence/AC/impact/recommendation/confidence, individual design disposition/resolution, human/contract flags, supplementary requirements and unresolved implementation status. No finding is relabeled as remediated merely because this document proposes a fix.
- [Original independent results](006-independent-architecture-review-results.md) and all original output/transcript/receipt hashes remain evidence of REVIEW_FAIL. A new review verdict must come from genuinely fresh isolated provider sessions.

## Accepted human decisions

META-01 is accepted as the v1 disclosure contract: current human approval is bound to dataset/environment, institute, entity, field and exact persisted value; professional instructor identity is approved metadata only; join code is never disclosed; descriptions/announcement content/material descriptions stay blank; coverImage stays blank/local placeholder; changed/unapproved values fail closed; no omission/truncation or rejected-value API/RSC/error/log disclosure. Operational identities not supplied by the human remain required assignments, never invented.

Pathname markers are removed from the authorization design. Middleware may retain routing/security-header assistance but is not changed or trusted as final authority. Actual server session, explicit role, server route parameters and independently guarded pages/layouts/API/actions/services decide authority.

Successful oversight read and access audit use one scoped interactive database transaction; only its committed result can be serialized. No database-immutability or universal legacy-403 audit claim is added.

SUPER_USER account support is exactly existing login, logout and `/api/auth/me` own identity. No profile/settings/password/session/notification/OAuth/admin support exception is added. Public leaderboard stays anonymous and unchanged under U-01; remove its modification-eligible entry and do not add optional actor-specific denial there.

Normal-role authority is role AND persisted relationship/ownership AND actual institute. PROFESSOR/TEACHER/INSTRUCTOR are canonical instructor aliases; unknown fails closed; input actorId/permissions/header claims never elevate; all children resolve through the actual persisted authorized parent. Existing legitimate domain behavior is preserved; unsafe cross-resource access is not treated as legitimate regression behavior.

## Role and authentication contract

Recognized roles: STUDENT, canonical INSTRUCTOR (PROFESSOR/TEACHER/INSTRUCTOR aliases), ADMIN and explicit SUPER_USER. All other values resolve to unauthorized UNKNOWN, never STUDENT or Admin. SUPER_USER is an oversight-only capability with a hard legacy ceiling independent of persisted User.permissions. RequireAdmin remains ADMIN-only; legacy permissions and role-management matrices use the separate ADMIN/INSTRUCTOR/STUDENT managed-role set. Public registration/bulk/role-change inputs never silently normalize an invalid role into a granted role or expose SUPER_USER as a new selectable provisioning option.

One canonical actor is selected once per request/invocation from real cookie/Bearer session data. Preserve valid-cookie precedence and existing HTTP Bearer fallback when the cookie path fails; missing/expired/inactive result is 401. Server actions obtain actual Next request headers/context and use the same resolver, rather than combining a cookie-selected user with a Bearer-selected role. Transitional session-id compatibility is not silently removed. No X-Role/X-User-Id/program/ownerId/query claim participates in authority. A passed plain object or input.actorId is not an authenticated actor; direct service/action entries reauthenticate and bind to real actor.id.

For actor/resource decisions inside an oversight transaction, revalidate the chosen actual session ID/user/expiry/active role and relevant institute in that transaction; never switch to a different credential or cached user's permissions. Normal-role helpers use the same identity rule. Review token-conflict cases individually: valid/valid, valid/invalid, invalid/valid, expired, revoked, inactive and transitional IDs. No new auth-policy migration is claimed as implemented.

## Header-free page, shell and RSC protection

The common `(dashboard)/[institute]/layout.tsx` verifies the real session and explicit supported institute parameters, then chooses a shell by role **before legacy eligibility/enrollment/gamification/notification reads**. SUPER_USER gets only AcademicOperationsShell with own identity, scope selection, oversight navigation and logout. Normal actors retain their appropriate existing shell and institute scoping. The post-login Super User destination starts at ICS; an explicitly requested institute root redirects to that same supported institute's academic operations, and explicit IBE/ITE oversight URLs retain their requested institute. Selector changes route only, never User.instituteId or Session; detail switch goes to target institute list, dropping foreign courseId. Existing home-portal credential validation is not loosened merely to choose the initial post-login destination.

This common layout is **not sufficient to protect children**. Next can render child segments independently/concurrently. Every one of the 78 existing dashboard page/layout files is enumerated in the matrix. Every legacy server page/layout starts with an explicit capability check using actual session + its own params and operation before protected reads, computing/serializing props, invoking sensitive services or returning JSX children. SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN is denied at each legacy leaf. The root landing redirect and common shell branch are explicitly distinguished. Existing course layouts require recognized role plus actual course/institute and assignment/enrollment, before pending submission counts or headers/tabs.

The only current client page (`activities/sandbox/page.tsx`) receives a future server wrapper at its existing page path. Extract its existing client content into the explicitly allowlisted `legacy-client.tsx`; authenticate/deny at the server wrapper before returning that component. Preserve legitimate normal-role props/behavior. Other route client components remain behind guarded server pages and their own guarded APIs/actions. A downloadable JS bundle is not permission to fetch private data.

Dedicated oversight layout/page/list/detail each independently authenticates SUPER_USER using server params and invokes the authorized service; they never mount the old course layout or learning components. No authorization check needs a pathname header or pathname inferred from the browser. New APIs and actions always independently authorize even if the user bypasses the page.

Direct navigation and refresh execute guarded server leaves. Prefetch/RSC requests execute the same guarded leaves and services; they receive no private props before successful capability/metadata/audit checks. Rewrites execute the actual destination's server params/capability, so a rewrite or caller header cannot change role/resource authority. Unsupported or encoded parameters fail the supported-institute check; course queries include actual institute. Server actions authenticate at invocation and re-resolve closure/bound arguments; page render authorization does not authorize action replay. All six inline actions have distinct invocation cases. No private DTO is streamed from a suspended child, cached in a shared identity scope, passed through a raw error boundary or serialized before the service has returned successfully.

Region `course-supervision-readonly` retains the exact approved title heading and no buttons/form/editable/mutation/execution controls. Scope/logout controls sit outside it. Allowed links stay same-origin within selected academic operations. No legacy sidebar/mobile More/Admin fallback/profile/settings/notification/gamification/KX/Calendar widgets mount for SUPER_USER. Pure shell components receive only the approved DTO and own basic identity, not full Session/User/Course records.

## META-01 exact disclosure and operational contract

DTO key shapes remain those in the seven frozen files. Every retained mutable string—including course/event/material titles, course catalog code/subject/section/room, institutional name, event type, and professional instructor id/name projection—requires a current approval bound to its exact persisted value/relationship. No approval can authorize courseCode, assessment content or a student identity as an instructor. The v1 blank description/content/coverImage rules apply even if an approval entry tries to populate them. IDs/dates/types are scoped technical scalars, not a free-text escape channel. MATERIAL-only queries exclude assessment rows, attachments, targets, attempts, submissions and answers.

Approvals live in the proposed **server-only** `apps/web/src/institutes/oversight-metadata/approved-metadata.json`, validated by the proposed `src/lib/academic-oversight-metadata.ts`. These are exact future allowlist paths, not files created now. They use the existing reviewed repository/configuration process; no schema, signing service, harness-key or deployment-mechanism change is introduced. No client component may import the manifest/helper; independent build/import-graph verification must prove it stays out of client/RSC payloads. A server-only mechanism must remain compatible with the unchanged Node fixture bootstrap; do not introduce an unresolved package/conditional import that breaks the frozen direct-action suite.

An approval includes policy version, dataset/environment identity, institute ID/code, entity kind/ID, field, exact UTF-8 SHA-256 (no normalization), relevant instructor relationship/current role/active state, human approval reference/issued time/expiry/revocation status. Hashes are not encryption or anonymization. Never accept approval claims from request fields, User.permissions, a HARNESS flag, an ordinary course editor or a forged file path.

Operational decisions:

| Item | Required contract / current assignment |
|---|---|
| Trusted academic/privacy approver | A real institution-designated human, named through human governance before any production disclosure. **Identity not supplied; REQUIRED HUMAN ASSIGNMENT.** Agent is not an approver. |
| Manifest maintainer/release reviewer | Trusted existing repository/config maintainer accountable for approved versions. **Identity not supplied; REQUIRED HUMAN ASSIGNMENT.** No self-approved production entries. |
| Location / default | Exact server-only JSON path above; absent/unconfigured/invalid manifest is deny-by-default. No production values or approvals are authored here. |
| Dataset binding | Server-owned environment/dataset ID and trusted target fingerprint must match the actual configured database/environment. Disposable fixture bindings can never authorize production. Actual production ID/fingerprint and attestation procedure are **REQUIRED HUMAN/OPERATOR ASSIGNMENTS**, not invented aliases. Credentials/URLs are never emitted in approvals or reports. |
| Expiry | Every entry requires issued/expiresAt; expired or future-issued entries fail. Human owner must choose a review lifetime appropriate to actual data; no perpetual/default auto-approval. Admission requires validity through the bounded transaction deadline. |
| Revocation | Versioned reviewed manifest with explicit revoked entries/current version. It is pinned immutably for a request; coordinated publication invalidates future admissions, and in-flight results recheck current version/expiry before delivery. If consistent version/expiry checks cannot be established, withhold result and stop rather than claim immediate atomic revocation across DB/config. Owner/runbook is a required operational assignment. |

Complete deterministic arrays remain mandatory. Missing approval for any required scoped active record fails the whole read; never drop or truncate courses/events/materials. Edited/moved records, changed role/active/instructor association, revoked/expired/wrong-dataset entries invalidate approval. The runtime service validates approval on the scoped values it actually read. Publication and in-flight revocation limitations must be reviewed explicitly; no semantic privacy or cross-system atomicity claim is inferred from value hashes.

The exact benign generated fixture titles/instructor IDs can retain their original heading assertions when separate independently reviewed dummy approval records are bound to the disposable fixture dataset/current values. Original seven fixtures stay unchanged. Separate fixture support is future work only after actual architecture PASS and independent artifact review; no automatic production approval from the frozen seeder or dummy identity is introduced.

## Exact successful-read audit transaction

Use the existing `{db}` singleton with PrismaPg/pg Pool, not a new client or database backend. Intended call: interactive `db.$transaction(callback, {isolationLevel: 'RepeatableRead', maxWait: 5000, timeout: 10000})`. This is a proposed implementation contract, not a transaction executed in this task.

Inside the callback, use **tx only** for session/user revalidation, selected Institute, active scoped Course/related records and AuditLog insert. Do not call a helper that writes through global db or an independent Pool. No parallel/global cached query, external executor/network request or streaming side effect in the callback. RepeatableRead supplies a single database snapshot for authorization/resource/data consistency; it does not promise instant observation of a revocation committed after snapshot admission. The chosen actor/session is checked in the same snapshot, and no alternative identity is selected.

Order:

1. Validate canonical actor/SUPER_USER capability and supported server-selected institute; acquire the controlled transaction and revalidate the actual session/user.
2. Resolve Institute and active Course with actual institute predicate; read only allowlisted fields/related records using tx. No courseCode selection or student/grade/attempt/answer data query.
3. Validate all required current metadata approvals against this exact snapshot and request-pinned approval version; construct the entire DTO server-locally. Any denial/projection/approval failure throws before ALLOWED insert and results in rollback/no DTO.
4. Insert the required AuditLog through tx with only actor/self target, exact action, selected institute, scoped courseId for detail and outcome ALLOWED. Do not log rejected/raw descriptive values or approval details.
5. Await the **whole** `$transaction` promise, including successful COMMIT. Only then may the route/page receive a successful DTO and serialize/render it. Revalidate approval-version/expiry admission before delivering; any ambiguity withholds result. No shared cache or stream of data before this await.

List action is SUPER_USER_ACADEMIC_OVERSIGHT_READ; detail is SUPER_USER_COURSE_SUPERVISION_READ. adminId and targetId both equal the actual Super User; metadata remains a JSON-encoded String as in the schema. A safe failure exposes neither DTO nor private RSC body. Existing audit rows are never updated/deleted; no database-level immutability or universal new legacy-403 audit is claimed.

ALLOWED records a successfully authorized audited read attempt, not guaranteed network delivery. A connection failure/ambiguous COMMIT produces no DTO and no automatic transaction replay; an audit may already be committed. Do not assert it rolled back without evidence or retry into duplicate audit rows. Client network/render failure after commit cannot be atomically rolled back with the DB. Review these delivery/commit boundaries explicitly.

Source-level transaction feasibility is established against the installed 7.9.1 adapter/client: `PrismaPgAdapter.startTransaction` acquires a pool connection and executes BEGIN/SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL; `options.usePhantomQuery=false`; the installed Prisma client transaction manager emits COMMIT/ROLLBACK SQL and awaits transaction completion; adapter commit/rollback releases that connection. Existing bulkAssignInstructor already uses interactive tx. No runtime atomicity, rollback or connection-failure test has been run here. If the future service cannot preserve tx-only queries/write, await commit and safe failure with this adapter, stop and report the exact limitation; do not describe a separate global createAuditLog call as transactional.

## Exact critical-boundary rules

The JSON matrix is the operation-level source of truth; rules below clarify special cases and prevent generic “add a guard” remediation:

- **Generic course reads:** actor role is STUDENT with actual APPROVED Enrollment, instructor alias with Course.instructorId=actor.id, or ADMIN system authority; non-Admin home institute equals actual course. Query children through that course, including syllabusItemId/submissionId mismatch checks; students see own submissions only, instructors/Admin only the authorized course. SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN returns 403 before private reads.
- **Teaching/grading/enrollment/groups/attachments:** actual instructor alias + assigned course + institute or ADMIN; every group/member/announcement/item/submission/grade rule/template belongs to the same authorized parent. Student work requires STUDENT + enrollment + own submission; attachmentId belongs to that actual submission. No parent ID supplied for revalidation can authorize an unrelated child. Grading, notifications, EXP/badges, deletion and cache work follow the checks.
- **Creation and auto-assignment:** instructor course creation is allowed in actual home institute and assigns the real actor. `bulkAssignInstructor` permits ADMIN authority or instructor self-assignment only to an actual course already owned/just created by the actor, with actual target role/institute checks. This preserves the current instructorCreateCourse call chain; an Admin-only helper would otherwise break legitimate creation. Generated join codes require recognized teaching/Admin creation capability, never SUPER_USER.
- **Workspace:** personal note/task/event writes require actual creator ownership and institute. Shared course scheduling requires assigned instructor/Admin and actual linked course; students cannot edit shared teaching schedules. All SUPER_USER workspace operations are denied before parse/read/write. No Calendar redesign is authorized.
- **Activities/CodeLab/Judge0:** ICS from persisted institute, never a program claim; SUPER_USER/UNKNOWN denied first. Own freeform code execution uses actor-owned input/session with recognized legacy role. Persisted template/assessment execution additionally requires real course enrollment/assignment/Admin and actual owned attempt. Student submission/progress/milestone uses real owned prior work and same enrolled course; supplied score/title/seed/studentId is not authority. Instructor rejection resolves ActivitySubmission→Template→Course and target member; alert/commend without courseId must infer an actual shared assigned course, not accept user existence alone. All execution siblings, alias invalidation, fallback/rate-limit/template/EXP/grade paths share this boundary.
- **Inline actions:** each createTemplate/saveTemplate authenticates at invocation and resolves its closure Course/template/item through persisted assignment/institute before parsing JSON, creating/updating assessment records, revalidation or redirects. Each of six closures has an explicit real compiled-action replay case.
- **Callable skills:** reauthenticate actual actor at every exported use-server entry; actorId must equal real actor or fail. Bulk ingestion is Admin-only; bulk assignment has the explicit authenticated creation/self-assignment rule above; enrollment/group helpers require real course authority; generated code requires creation capability; pure flagSentiment may compute only a recognized legacy caller's input and cannot remain a public server-action escape. No fake system-user bypass is added.
- **Gradebook:** guarded exportGradebookSkill authenticates and validates assignment/institute/Admin before roster/grade Promise.all. A caller-created authorization context or courseId alone is not a guard. All grade edits/upserts/clear/policy/export also resolve submission/item/student through that actual course.
- **GitHub:** actual actor and owned GithubToken first; never another user's token. Post/submission/comment/RepoLink/CI references resolve through actual course/post relationship and stored cohort/instructor/anonymous visibility. Mutations require owned link/author and appropriate student submission or instructor/Admin authority. Course-linked owner/repo/ref/path must match actual authorized link before outbound calls. Preserve legitimate standalone repository discovery using only the actor's own persisted token and provider permission; it cannot authorize private course/student records. Similarity/snapshot jobs run only after actual owned enrollment/item/link checks. Webhook remains separate existing signature/dedup service authority, unchanged.
- **Public/support:** anonymous leaderboard/health/institutes and webhook are reviewed-but-unchanged exceptions. Login/logout/me are exact Super User support. Authenticated SUPER_USER cannot use profile/settings/change-password/refresh/sessions/notifications/OAuth or public recovery/register paths to obtain management rights. Truly anonymous recovery/register protocol remains unchanged. CORS/OPTIONS grants no resource capability. Admin reauthentication and existing audit actions remain intact.

For protected operations, missing/invalid/inactive authentication is 401, denied role/capability is 403, and absent/foreign/non-owned parent/child is a uniform safe 404. Server pages safely redirect unauthenticated users to login and deny wrong-role legacy pages without private props; direct actions return/throw actual authorization failure in their existing contract. Body validation, 404-from-missing function, Next CSRF rejection, generic 500 or unchanged DB alone does not count as role-denial verification. Existing source contracts are retained for legitimately authorized actors.

## Exact file and verification scope

008 allowlist retains exact before hashes, adds all required legacy page leaves and the single client extraction, removes middleware/public leaderboard from write eligibility and proposes metadata validation/configuration files. No application source is modified to match this plan. The seven frozen files, root Prisma schema/migrations, dependencies, packages, apps/api/mobile/desktop, harness code/policies/configs, provider state and closed runtime-repair artifacts remain forbidden. Existing host-only preparation dispatcher is separate from product source and does not change a gate.

Future verification must bind unique CASE IDs from every one of the 171 HTTP method/alias operations, 59 exported/inline/service boundaries and 78 server page/layout leaves. Independently verify derived HEAD behavior for GET routes and unsupported method behavior; no wildcard row or group test title establishes per-operation coverage. Compare exact inventory/case sets, detect missing/duplicate/import/validation-only cases, retain individual operation evidence and both positive normal-role and negative Super User/unknown/foreign/other-owner expectations. Inline actions use actual compiled replay; protocol failures are not substitutes. Exact source hashes and case-set digest must enter the future plan and reviewed supplementary assertions.

Add future metadata approval/contamination/expiry/revocation/wrong-dataset/changed-value cases, exact transaction success/audit-write failure/rollback/ambiguous-commit-withheld-result cases, actor-token selection/alias cases and direct navigation/RSC/prefetch/rewrite/server-action page-leaf tests. Preserve the original three frozen Node cases and fourteen browser cases plus unchanged auth-setup dependency names. No new product tests are authored or executed now; all old command mappings remain NOT_EXECUTED.

## Corrected independent HTTP review coverage strategy

Original SU-REVIEW-HTTP received all 120 route bodies but returned no individual coverage for 110. Preserve its output and disputed source-absence claim; do not relabel it a complete review. New HTTP requests partition the 120 **explicit paths** into disjoint hash-bound subsets with every declared/aliased verb, original source hash, line-numbered sanitized bodies, exact assigned matrix rows and shared policy evidence. Each reviewer sees only its own assigned subset and shared necessary context, never other reviewers' private output.

Each fresh isolated reviewer must return one coverage record for every assigned path with all its declared/aliased methods and relevant authority classification, source/request binding, exact evidence, severity/AC/impact/recommendation/confidence, human/contract flags and limitations. No wildcard paths, inferred author-reviewed records, omitted methods or copied old reviewer verdicts. Compare output coverage to assigned path+verb set; missing coverage fails regardless of verdict. Aggregate all independently authored findings under request/session-qualified IDs without silently deduplicating disagreements. Existing route scopes not in a subset are assigned to other reviewers, not automatically missing from the overall package. Partition further only with explicit hash-bound subsets preserving the exact union.

Actions/service and shell/metadata/audit receive fresh isolated reviews of their respective revised boundaries. A revised design's review is not source implementation validation, nor formal Red-Team acceptance. Current next harness stage remains requirements. Do not fabricate predecessor artifacts, leases, signatures or accept a product PASS from preparation reviews.

## Remaining blockers and stopping conditions

All 28 original independent findings remain implementation-unresolved. Human decisions above settle design directions, not source fixes. This revised proposal needs fresh independent architecture assessment and complete HTTP path/method coverage. Operational approver/maintainer/dataset/expiry/publication assignments are still required before production disclosure; deny-by-default is explicit until supplied. Transaction feasibility is source-supported, with runtime/error/delivery verification pending future authorization. Any remaining HIGH design defect, coverage gap, required contract revision or unsupported transaction/manifest semantics stops progression.

Fresh architecture PASS, if obtained, does not grant HIGH implementation approval, an implementation lease, formal predecessor acceptance or product validation. Supplementary test authorship waits for that actual independent PASS; separate test review/freeze and formal source-bound plan/preflight stages remain later gates. 1: # Preflight verification contract, not feature implementation approval
2: 
3: These fixtures are a proposed verification interface for the human's twelve criteria. The later requirements/recon/red-team/architecture adjudication must accept or explicitly revise the endpoint/DTO/UI/audit contract before authoritative planning. Any revision requires fresh independent fixture review and a new exact-source preflight receipt. No fixture approval means that the feature exists, product tests pass or HIGH implementation is approved.
4: 
5: HTTP GET interfaces: `/api/academic-oversight/{ics|ibe|ite}/courses` and `/api/academic-oversight/{institute}/courses/{courseId}`. The read-only page is `/{institute}/academic-operations/courses/{courseId}/supervision`; its course-only region has `data-testid="course-supervision-readonly"`. Exact response shapes are enforced by fixture.ts. Course metadata, assigned instructor id/name, course-linked calendar summaries, announcements and syllabus/material summaries are allowed. Student objects/identities, grades, submissions, attempts, answers, execution details and additional fields are not allowed.
6: 
7: Program scope is grounded in the existing repository. There is no Program model. `src/lib/activity-eligibility.ts` explicitly uses ICS as the current BSIT/BSCpE eligibility boundary. The tests therefore reject caller-supplied program/institute claims on the real activity endpoint and verify request claims cannot alter selected-institute route scope. They do not invent program tables, memberships or a new permission model.
8: 
9: Real HTTP mutation contracts: POST/PATCH/DELETE `/api/workspace/events` (courseId/id/title/eventDate); POST `/api/courses/{id}/submissions/grade` (submissionId/grade); PATCH `/api/courses/{id}/enrollments` (enrollmentId/action); POST `/api/activities/submit` (the actual shared schema); PATCH `/api/admin/users/{id}/status` (isActive) and `/role` (newRole/adminPassword). The role-escalation probe supplies the Super User's own generated test password so missing re-auth input cannot masquerade as authorization. These are existing paths; 404 or validation failure cannot count as authorization denial. The real POST `/api/codelab/run` handler is called directly in the action suite with a fail-closed executor-boundary spy: authentication/eligibility are real, and any executor invocation fails the test without allowing public Judge0 or local fallback execution.
10: 
11: Course creation/editing, syllabus/material mutation, announcement mutation, student submission/attachment and server-side grading actions are directly imported and called by `tests/server/controlled/superuser-actions.test.mjs`. Only Next cookies/headers/cache context and the external execution boundary are adapted. The real session database lookup, role/eligibility checks, ownership checks, Prisma and teaching/student functions are not replaced. Fixtures include SUPER_USER enrollment, own submission and instructor assignment to expose accidental privilege inheritance. Normal-role ownership negatives use existing guarded course-edit and grading contracts rather than inventing a new program/role domain.
12: 
13: `AuditLog.metadata` is a String in the existing schema. Access audit assertions safely support that representation. The proposed successful Super User list/detail actions are `SUPER_USER_ACADEMIC_OVERSIGHT_READ` / `SUPER_USER_COURSE_SUPERVISION_READ`, with actor and target equal to the Super User and metadata `{institute, courseId (detail only), outcome:'ALLOWED'}`. Existing Admin account status mutations must preserve existing `ACCOUNT_SUSPENSION` / `ACCOUNT_REACTIVATION` audit records. Existing denied operations are captured as concrete controller-fixture request/action evidence (actor, scope, target, operation, status/result, timestamp, environment and before/after hashes). No new application audit policy for every legacy 403 is silently imposed. A later architecture decision may require additional application denial audits; that decision and updated fixtures must then be reviewed.
14: 
15: Every public base table is fingerprinted around denied Super User mutations, except append-only AuditLog and migration bookkeeping. Existing audit rows are separately checked for preservation. This covers identity/role/session changes, teaching data, schedules, material targets and attachments, submissions, grades, enrollments, attempts, assessment answers, notifications and gamification side effects.
16: 
17: Host setup: install the unchanged schema only into an empty uniquely owned loopback PostgreSQL `harness_*` database; execute `seed-fixture.cjs --root <clean checkout> --out <host-private absolute file>`. It rejects non-empty databases and live-env checkouts and generates dummy opaque sessions. Keep the resulting JSON outside agent context. For harness-runner commands, write a version-1 `.orchestra/runs/<runId>/lms-fixture-locator.json` with `{version:1,runId,file,sha256}`; the existing runner already supplies HARNESS_RUN_ID, HARNESS_TEST_DATABASE_URL and HARNESS_TEST_BASE_URL, so no gate/env-forwarding change is needed.
18: 
19: The existing harness-private browser configuration owns server startup and evidence capture; it must not be replaced. Its unchanged auth-setup project reads `tests/e2e/fixtures/test-accounts.ts`; that verification fixture now obtains controlled dummy login accounts through the verified host-private locator, while ordinary developer tests retain their previous env/default behavior. This avoids changing the runner's env allowlist (which does not forward E2E_INSTRUCTOR). The controlled browser suite clears inherited storage and uses its own opaque role tokens. No HTTP browser case calls the execution endpoint. The direct handler suite's executor spy asserts zero invocations and blocks both public Judge0 and in-process fallbacks if a guard regresses. This is an external dependency fixture, not a replacement for session/role/eligibility checks.
20: 
21: Future validation commands, after actual HIGH approval and implementation:
22: 
23: - Browser/direct HTTP through the unchanged compiled adapter: `pnpm exec playwright test tests/e2e/controlled/superuser-oversight.spec.ts --config .orchestra/harness/playwright.config.ts` (existing private configuration, one worker, no retries/only, JSON evidence).
24: - Direct actions: `node --import ./tests/server/controlled/bootstrap.mjs --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-reporter ./scripts/harness/test-reporter.cjs tests/server/controlled/superuser-actions.test.mjs`. The fixture bootstrap selects the existing app tsconfig and initializes real AsyncLocalStorage before registering the installed tsx loader. The action suite uses Next's actual request/cache storage and proves real session lookup for each active role before testing denials. No auth/domain module is mocked for alias resolution. Only the external execution client export is replaced with an asserted fail-closed spy, then restored at shutdown.
25: - All ten security-boundary coverage names are retained. All product validation, QA, security, code review and release gates remain required.
26: 
27: Current readiness work may typecheck/list the fixture suites and validate dummy seed contracts. It must not execute these product assertions as a passing feature run before implementation or claim RELEASE_READY.
